title: Egyptian Mythology Archive
scope: Historical reference database; not lessons or initiation. Source links provide research context; record-level scholarly review remains ongoing.

context: Divine Egypt — Metropolitan Museum of Art
set: Nubt, cult center of Seth — UCL
seti: Offering table of Seti I — Met
lavey: The age of Satanism — Oxford Academic

records.title: Osiris
records.description: Mummiform ruler of the dead, husband of Isis and father of Horus in the familiar Osirian cycle. His restoration after death underlies the identification of the deceased with Osiris. Abydos and Busiris were major centers.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Isis
records.description: Uses protective knowledge to recover Osiris and safeguard Horus; throne sign and later cow horns mark her images. Her worship spread widely across the Mediterranean.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Horus
records.description: Falcon deity with multiple local and genealogical forms; the living king was identified with Horus, while Horus son of Isis contests Seth for sovereignty.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Set
records.description: Brother and rival of Osiris in the Ennead; an adversary of Horus but also a defender of the sun against Apep. Worship, iconography and political fortunes changed across regions and dynasties. See the dedicated Set dossier.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Nephthys
records.description: Sister of Isis, Osiris and Seth in the Ennead; appears with Isis protecting the deceased. Her relationship to Seth and Anubis differs across traditions.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Ra
records.description: Solar deity whose daily journey renews the cosmos; associated with Heliopolis and many composite gods. Solar theology includes dawn, midday and evening forms.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Atum
records.description: Heliopolitan self-originating creator associated with the first emergence from primordial waters, father of Shu and Tefnut in major traditions.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Shu
records.description: Separates Nut from Geb, making the inhabited world possible; paired with Tefnut in the Ennead.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Tefnut
records.description: Paired with Shu and mother of Geb and Nut; participates in traditions about the departure and return of the solar goddess.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Geb
records.description: Earth deity beneath Nut; father of the later Ennead generation and associated with royal succession.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Nut
records.description: Arches over the world; receives the sun and gives birth to it again in solar imagery. Her body also shelters the deceased.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Anubis
records.description: Canid deity associated with necropolises, mummification and the protection of the body; guides or supervises judgment scenes.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Thoth
records.description: Ibis or baboon deity associated with sacred writing, measurement, lunar cycles and adjudication; principal god at Hermopolis.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Ma'at
records.description: Personification of the balanced order upheld by divine and human action; a feather identifies her in judgment iconography.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Hathor
records.description: Cow or woman with horns and solar disk; associated with Dendera, celebration, the western necropolis and solar Eye traditions.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Sekhmet
records.description: Lioness deity whose destructive power could also protect; linked to Ptah and Nefertum at Memphis.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Bastet
records.description: Feline goddess of Bubastis; earlier lioness forms and later domestic-cat imagery express differing aspects of her power.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Ptah
records.description: Memphite creator associated with artisans; the Shabaka Stone relates creation through the heart and tongue.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Amun
records.description: Theban god whose political prominence grew in the New Kingdom; Amun-Re combines his identity with solar theology.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Mut
records.description: Major Theban goddess and partner of Amun; frequently represented with the double crown or lioness aspects.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Khonsu
records.description: Lunar deity of the Theban triad, child of Amun and Mut; associated with time and healing in later traditions.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Khepri
records.description: Scarab-associated solar manifestation expressing emergence and transformation.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Aten
records.description: Promoted under Akhenaten as the central focus of royal worship; rays terminate in hands bestowing life. The Amarna reform was historically exceptional.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Sobek
records.description: Crocodile god particularly prominent in the Fayum and Kom Ombo; dangerous strength could protect ruler and land.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Khnum
records.description: Ram god of Elephantine and Esna; shaping living beings on a potter's wheel is characteristic of his creative imagery.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Satet
records.description: Elephantine goddess linked to the southern boundary and flood waters; associated with Khnum and Anuket.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Anuket
records.description: Goddess of the First Cataract region, associated with Elephantine and the southern river landscape.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Hapy
records.description: Personifies the yearly inundation and its agricultural abundance; not the similarly named son of Horus.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Min
records.description: Ithyphallic god prominent at Coptos and Akhmim; associated with reproduction, royal festivals and expeditions.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Montu
records.description: Falcon-associated warrior god of the Theban region, notably Armant and Tod.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Neith
records.description: Goddess prominent at Sais; creator in Esna theology and guardian in funerary contexts. Her functions span different traditions.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Serqet
records.description: Scorpion-associated goddess invoked for protection; one of the goddesses guarding funerary equipment.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Nekhbet
records.description: Vulture goddess of Elkab and royal protector, paired with Wadjet as the Two Ladies.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Wadjet
records.description: Cobra goddess of the Delta, linked to the uraeus and the royal Two Ladies title.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Bes
records.description: Frontal dwarf-like protective figure, often represented with leonine features; appears on domestic objects and birth-related imagery.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Taweret
records.description: Composite hippopotamus figure with protective associations in domestic and birth contexts.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Heka
records.description: Divine personification of the power that enables effective speech and action; magic belongs within Egyptian religion rather than outside it.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Sia
records.description: Personified understanding or perception, frequently associated with the solar entourage.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Hu
records.description: Personification of effective utterance, connected with creation and the solar bark.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Nefertum
records.description: Youthful lotus-associated deity linked to solar emergence and the Memphite divine family.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Imhotep
records.description: Historical official of Djoser later divinized; his healing cult flourished particularly in later Egypt.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Amenhotep son of Hapu
records.description: New Kingdom official later revered as a divine intermediary, especially in the Theban region.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Seshat
records.description: Goddess of recording and architectural measurement, prominent in royal foundation imagery.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Meretseger
records.description: Cobra-associated goddess linked to the Theban western mountain and the community of royal tomb workers.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Renenutet
records.description: Cobra goddess linked with agricultural abundance, nourishment and protection of the child.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Shai
records.description: Personified fate, appearing in birth and judgment contexts; sometimes associated with Renenutet and Meskhenet.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Meskhenet
records.description: Birth-associated goddess whose emblem relates to birthing bricks; appears in contexts of determining destiny.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Heqet
records.description: Frog-associated goddess connected with childbirth and the renewal of life.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Wosret
records.description: Theban goddess associated with royal names and divine protection; not simply interchangeable with Mut.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Bat
records.description: Early bovine goddess with distinctive inward-curving horns, later closely associated with Hathor.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Pakhet
records.description: Lioness goddess worshipped near Beni Hasan, where rock-cut sanctuaries attest her cult.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Maahes
records.description: Lion deity associated with divine protection and later feline goddess cults.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Menhit
records.description: Lioness goddess especially connected with Esna traditions and the solar protective complex.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Werethekau
records.description: Divine embodiment of great magical power, associated with crowns and protection of the ruler.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Nehebkau
records.description: Serpent deity with protective and nourishing roles in funerary traditions; not synonymous with Apep.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Mehen
records.description: Protective serpent coils around the solar deity in netherworld imagery.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Apep
records.description: Serpent threatening the solar journey, regularly defeated but returning; unlike Seth, he primarily embodies opposition to cosmic renewal.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Ammit
records.description: Composite creature associated with the failed heart-weighing, combining crocodile, lion and hippopotamus features.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Wepwawet
records.description: Canid deity of Asyut, associated with processions and opening routes for the king and deceased.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Khentiamentiu
records.description: Early Abydene deity or designation meaning foremost of the westerners; later strongly associated with Osiris.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Sokar
records.description: Memphite funerary god associated with the desert cemetery and later Ptah-Sokar-Osiris forms.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Andjety
records.description: Busiris-associated god whose attributes became connected with Osiris.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Banebdjedet
records.description: Ram deity of Mendes with associations to Osiris and other gods in composite theology.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Hatmehit
records.description: Fish goddess of Mendes, associated with Banebdjedet in local traditions.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Neper
records.description: Personification of grain and agricultural sustenance; linked with fertility and renewal.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Hesat
records.description: Bovine goddess associated with nourishment and divine milk, including funerary contexts.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Mekhit
records.description: Lioness goddess linked with Onuris in local traditions, part of a wider complex of protective solar goddesses.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Onuris
records.description: Warrior god of Thinis and Sebennytos, linked with bringing back a distant goddess.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Resheph
records.description: Levantine deity incorporated into Egyptian worship, especially in the New Kingdom; illustrates cross-cultural religious exchange.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Anat
records.description: Levantine goddess adopted in Egypt; associated with royal warfare and Seth in some New Kingdom contexts.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Astarte
records.description: Levantine goddess adopted into Egyptian religion; participates in traditions of conflict and divine kingship.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Qadesh
records.description: Goddess depicted in New Kingdom imagery alongside Min and Resheph; the interpretation of her origins and identity is debated.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Dedun
records.description: God associated with Nubia and southern products, particularly incense, in Egyptian religious texts.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Tutu
records.description: Late Period and Greco-Roman protective deity often shown as a composite sphinx; associated with controlling harmful forces.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Harpocrates
records.description: Child form of Horus, frequently with finger at mouth. Greek interpretations of the gesture as silence are later reception.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Horakhty
records.description: Horus form associated with the horizons, prominently combined with Ra as Ra-Horakhty.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Horus the Elder
records.description: An elder form of Horus, distinguished from the child of Isis in some mythic genealogies; prominent at Kom Ombo.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Imsety
records.description: Human-headed son of Horus, generally associated with the liver and Isis in standard later canopic arrangements.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Hapy son of Horus
records.description: Baboon-headed guardian generally associated with lungs and Nephthys, distinct from the inundation god.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Duamutef
records.description: Jackal-headed son of Horus, generally linked with the stomach and Neith.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Qebehsenuef
records.description: Falcon-headed son of Horus, generally linked with intestines and Serqet.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Nun
records.description: Pre-creation watery expanse, personified as a deity; remains beyond the ordered world after creation.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Naunet
records.description: Female counterpart of Nun within the Hermopolitan Ogdoad.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Heh
records.description: Male figure of the Ogdoad associated with indefinite extent and innumerable years.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Hauhet
records.description: Female counterpart of Heh in the Ogdoad.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Kek
records.description: Primordial darkness personified among the Ogdoad.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Kauket
records.description: Female counterpart of Kek in the Ogdoad.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Amunet
records.description: Female counterpart of Amun in some Ogdoad lists and a goddess worshipped at Thebes.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Tenenet
records.description: Local goddess associated with childbirth and the Armant divine circle.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Raet-Tawy
records.description: Female solar deity of the Two Lands, associated with Montu in Theban cults.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Qebehut
records.description: Serpent-associated goddess linked with cooling and refreshment of the dead, often described as Anubis's daughter.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Mafdet
records.description: Early feline or mongoose-like deity associated with protection against venomous creatures and royal justice; exact animal identification is debated.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Ash
records.description: Early god associated with western desert and Libyan regions; sometimes portrayed in animal-headed forms.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Nemty
records.description: Falcon-associated deity connected with Middle Egyptian local worship and divine ferrying in myth.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Babi
records.description: Baboon-associated deity of threatening vitality, appearing in mortuary and protective contexts.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Aker
records.description: Earth deity represented by paired lions or a double-headed figure, associated with the passage of the sun below the horizon.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Iah
records.description: Lunar deity whose identity sometimes overlaps with Thoth and Khonsu; appears in personal and royal names.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Sopdet
records.description: Personifies Sirius, whose annual visibility was connected with calendrical and inundation symbolism.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Sah
records.description: Stellar figure associated with Orion and Osiris in funerary astronomy.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Apis
records.description: Living sacred bull of Memphis linked to Ptah; after death associated with Osiris-Apis, an important background to Serapis.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Mnevis
records.description: Sacred bull of Heliopolis associated with solar religion.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Buchis
records.description: Sacred bull associated with Montu, centered in Armant.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Serapis
records.description: Greco-Egyptian deity promoted in the Ptolemaic period, drawing on Osiris-Apis and Greek iconographic conventions.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Isis-Thermouthis
records.description: Later composite form bringing together Isis and the serpent goddess of nourishment.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Names and epithets of Seth
records.description: Different transliterations reflect Egyptian spellings and later linguistic traditions. Nubti associates him with Nubt. Epithets should be traced to particular monuments rather than treated as one timeless title list.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: The Seth animal
records.description: Characteristic curved snout, upright squared ears and stiff or forked tail. No single zoological identification is certain; proposals remain disputed.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Seth in the Ennead
records.description: In the standard Heliopolitan family Seth belongs to the children of Geb and Nut. The relationships of Isis, Osiris and Nephthys differ in emphasis between narratives.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Seth and the death of Osiris
records.description: Seth's violence against Osiris establishes the succession dispute and the conditions for funerary renewal. Surviving Egyptian allusions and later Greek retellings do not tell identical stories.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Contendings of Horus and Seth
records.description: Ramesside literary narrative depicts the gods debating kingship through trials, disputes and competing claims. It preserves humor and ambiguity as well as conflict; it is not the sole version of the myth.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Seth defends the solar bark
records.description: In solar religion Seth can use his formidable force to repel the chaos serpent. This role is evidence against reducing him to an Egyptian equivalent of Satan.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Nubt / Ombos near Naqada
records.description: Upper Egyptian town with a sanctuary dedicated to Seth; excavated objects provide evidence for actual cult rather than myth alone. Distinct from Kom Ombo further south.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Votive objects at Nubt
records.description: Faience and other temple finds attest the material expression of Seth worship. Object dates and provenance matter more than modern claims about secret orders.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Avaris and Seth
records.description: The eastern Delta city became associated with Seth and Levantine storm-god traditions during the Second Intermediate Period. His local cult continued to matter in Ramesside royal ideology.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Seth under Ramesside rulers
records.description: Nineteenth Dynasty royal names and dedications show that Seth could be an honored state deity. Seti I's offering table is a surviving example.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Peribsen and Khasekhemwy
records.description: Peribsen's serekh carries the Seth animal instead of the conventional Horus falcon. Khasekhemwy's royal emblem combines both; political reasons remain debated.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Horus and Seth as paired royal powers
records.description: The two gods can appear together binding or supporting royal authority. Conflict and cooperation are both part of the iconographic record.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Desert, storms and foreigners
records.description: Seth is connected with arid regions, storms and forces beyond settled order. Those associations are not evidence that every foreigner or desert god was regarded as evil.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Seth and Levantine storm gods
records.description: New Kingdom religious contact could align Seth with storm-god imagery from western Asia; local forms must be distinguished rather than collapsed into a single identity.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Seth in the western oases
records.description: Oasis traditions preserved protective aspects of Seth into periods when hostile interpretations became influential elsewhere. Regional evidence complicates any single timeline of demonization.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Later hostility to Seth
records.description: Some first-millennium sources increasingly depict Seth as an enemy and damage or replace his image. Other local contexts retain positive roles; the shift was not uniform.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Seth and Typhon
records.description: Greek authors could identify Seth with Typhon. Plutarch's account is valuable evidence for later interpretation, not a verbatim record of early Egyptian theology.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: What an ancient cult of Seth means
records.description: Cult in Egyptological usage refers to organized veneration of a deity, expressed through sanctuaries, offerings and festivals. There is no established single continuous secret Setian institution spanning antiquity and the modern era.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Seth is not Apep
records.description: Seth can threaten order yet also defend it. Apep is a recurring opponent of the sun; their roles cannot be treated as equivalent or as a simple good-versus-evil dualism.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Research trail for Seth
records.description: Herman te Velde's Seth, God of Confusion (1967) is a classic specialist study; compare it with archaeological records from Nubt, museum objects and recent regional work. Historical interpretations remain open to revision.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Heliopolitan creation
records.description: Atum emerges from the primordial waters and produces successive divine generations. The Ennead links creation to the later Osiris and Horus royal myths.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Memphite theology
records.description: Ptah brings things into being through conception and utterance in the surviving Memphite theological text. Its date of composition is debated; the extant stone is Kushite-period.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Hermopolitan Ogdoad
records.description: Four pairs of primordial gods represent conditions preceding creation; versions include an emerging mound, lotus or egg. The roster and details vary.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Theban creation
records.description: Theban theology emphasizes the hidden source of existence, frequently combining Amun with solar and other creator traditions.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Esna creation
records.description: Late temple inscriptions preserve elaborate local creation accounts involving Neith and Khnum; they demonstrate that creation theology continued developing.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Elephantine creation
records.description: Southern cult traditions associate Khnum with shaping bodies and the river's life-giving abundance, in a local divine family.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Primeval mound
records.description: The first land rising from the waters supplies an image of differentiation and the beginning of ordered existence; local sites claimed particular associations.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Solar lotus
records.description: Emergence of the sun from a lotus appears in creation imagery; the flower's daily cycle makes it a sign of renewal.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Cosmic egg
records.description: Some creation accounts describe the first sun emerging from an egg; the originating divine figures and circumstances vary by source.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Humanity from divine tears
records.description: Some texts link humanity's origin to the creator's tears through wordplay; this is not a single canonical account of human origins.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Separation of sky and earth
records.description: Shu holding Nut above Geb expresses the separation of heaven and earth and the formation of the living world's space.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: The solar journey
records.description: The sun crosses the sky and passes through the night realm, encountering dangers before renewed emergence. Different funerary compositions structure the voyage differently.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Death and restoration of Osiris
records.description: The slain ruler is restored sufficiently to father Horus and reign in the realm of the dead. Horus's succession ties the myth to royal continuity and funerary identity.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Isis and the secret name of Ra
records.description: A magical narrative describes Isis obtaining Ra's hidden name after he is bitten by a serpent. The tale explores divine knowledge, vulnerability and healing power.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: The Eye of Ra
records.description: A powerful female manifestation of the solar deity can be protective or destructive. The Eye's withdrawal and return are told in multiple local forms.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Destruction of mankind
records.description: When humanity rebels, the solar Eye is sent against it; the episode includes a stratagem using red-colored beer to avert further destruction and the subsequent withdrawal of Ra.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: The Distant Goddess
records.description: A goddess withdraws into distant lands and her return restores well-being; the personnel, landscape and ritual setting vary between accounts.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Injury and healing of Horus's eye
records.description: The contested eye is injured and restored in traditions about Horus and Seth. Its healed state becomes a powerful funerary and protective emblem.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Moon as restored eye
records.description: The changing moon could express injury, diminution and renewal; there were multiple lunar gods and explanations.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Unification of the Two Lands
records.description: Joining Upper and Lower Egypt is represented through paired plants, deities and crowns; myth and political symbolism mutually reinforce royal order.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Bennu bird
records.description: Heron-like bird of solar and Osirian associations, especially at Heliopolis; Greek phoenix traditions are not identical to the Egyptian figure.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Divine birth of kings
records.description: Temple reliefs present a ruler's conception and birth as divinely authorized, linking biological kingship to cosmic legitimacy.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Seven Hathors
records.description: Groups of Hathor figures appear in protective and fate-related narratives, including stories where a child's future is pronounced.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Tale of Two Brothers
records.description: New Kingdom tale combines family conflict, transformation, magical survival and royal succession. Its figures should not simply be equated with all cult gods bearing similar names.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Tale of the Shipwrecked Sailor
records.description: Middle Kingdom literary story of a voyager encountering a marvelous serpent and returning home; illustrates mythic imagery outside temple theology.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Famine Stela
records.description: Ptolemaic inscription retrospectively situates a famine and its resolution in Djoser's reign; valuable for later claims about Khnum and Elephantine, not contemporary Old Kingdom evidence.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Ma'at and isfet
records.description: Ma'at describes the world sustained through proper conduct and divine order; isfet denotes disruptive wrong or disorder. Egyptian thought is not reducible to modern moral dualism.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Duat
records.description: A divine landscape traversed by the sun and the dead, variously celestial, subterranean or liminal. Its topography changes across the textual corpus.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Amentet
records.description: The west is linked with sunset and cemeteries, personified in a goddess who receives the dead. It is not a precise synonym for every representation of the Duat.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Field of Reeds
records.description: An idealized agricultural landscape in funerary literature, presenting abundance and continued life after successful passage.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Field of Offerings
records.description: Mortuary landscape associated with sustenance and ritual provisions, sometimes connected with the Field of Reeds.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Ka
records.description: Aspect of life and identity sustained through offerings and cult; the term cannot be translated adequately as a single Western concept of soul.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Ba
records.description: Manifestation of a being's mobility and capacity to appear; funerary images may show the ba traveling and returning to the body.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Akh
records.description: Transfigured and effective deceased, achieved through successful mortuary transformation; also an agent in relations with the living.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Ren
records.description: The name preserves and identifies a person; inscription, remembrance and erasure have religious and social consequences.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Shut
records.description: The shadow is one of several aspects of a person represented in funerary literature.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Ib
records.description: Seat of thought, emotion and responsibility in Egyptian contexts; central to judgment imagery.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Khat
records.description: The physical remains of the deceased, preserved and ritually transformed in mortuary practice.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Sah
records.description: Term used for a ritually dignified or transformed body; distinct from the stellar deity Sah despite similar modern spelling.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Weighing of the heart
records.description: Chapter 125 imagery shows assessment of the deceased's heart in relation to Ma'at, often with Anubis, Thoth and Ammit. Manuscripts differ in details.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Declarations of innocence
records.description: The deceased addresses a group of divine judges with denials of wrongdoing. The statements vary by manuscript and are not a single universal Egyptian civil code.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Second death
records.description: Funerary texts seek protection against destruction, deprivation and repeated death; failure is represented in more than one way rather than a standardized eternal punishment system.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Gate guardians
records.description: Underworld and mortuary compositions present guarded thresholds and beings with specialized names. Knowledge of names is an important literary motif.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Egyptian demons and guardians
records.description: Modern Egyptological category for specialized beings who may harm or protect. They are not uniformly evil, and many operate under divine authority.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Seven arrows of Sekhmet
records.description: The dangerous agents associated with solar goddess traditions express illness and threat as well as the need for protection; names and groupings depend on the text.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Four Sons of Horus
records.description: A quartet of guardians associated with the protection of internal organs and the deceased; the familiar heads and organ assignments became standardized over time.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Effective ancestors
records.description: The dead could be addressed as continuing participants in household and social life, invoked for aid or resolution of difficulties.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Twelve hours of night
records.description: Some New Kingdom royal compositions divide the nocturnal passage into twelve regions or hours with distinctive inhabitants and transformations.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Pyramid Texts
records.description: Mortuary utterances first extensively attested in late Old Kingdom royal pyramids, concerned with ascent, protection and divine transformation. Individual texts continued in later use.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Coffin Texts
records.description: Collection attested particularly on Middle Kingdom coffins, developing and adapting earlier mortuary material; includes diverse maps and divine transformations.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Book of the Dead
records.description: Variable collection of funerary spells, especially on papyrus from the New Kingdom onward. Spell numbering is modern; no individual copy represents a universal complete scripture.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Book of the Dead spell 17
records.description: Important composition interweaves declarations and explanations of divine identities and episodes, showing the complexity of Egyptian theological interpretation.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Book of the Dead spell 6
records.description: Inscription associated with figurines that perform work for the deceased in the afterlife.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Heart scarab spell
records.description: Formula asks the heart not to testify against its owner in judgment; frequently associated with heart scarabs.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Book of the Dead spell 125
records.description: Describes entry into the judgment hall and declarations of innocence; accompanying images are major sources for funerary theology.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Amduat
records.description: New Kingdom royal underworld composition mapping the sun's nocturnal passage in twelve hours; includes the midnight renewal of solar life.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Book of Gates
records.description: New Kingdom composition organizing the nightly journey into regions marked by guarded gates, with divine and human inhabitants.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Book of Caverns
records.description: Royal funerary composition depicting divine beings, enemies and regeneration in regions of the underworld.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Book of the Earth
records.description: Late New Kingdom royal funerary imagery emphasizing solar rebirth, subterranean forces and the bodies of gods.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Book of Nut
aliases: Fundamentals of the Course of the Stars
records.description: Astronomical and mythological composition describing stellar and solar movements through the sky goddess.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Book of the Heavenly Cow
records.description: Royal funerary myth concerning Ra's withdrawal, the reorganization of the cosmos and the solar Eye's destructive power.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Book of Two Ways
records.description: Middle Kingdom coffin compositions depicting routes through the otherworld with fire, boundaries and dangerous beings.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Litany of Ra
records.description: New Kingdom royal funerary text invoking multiple manifestations of the solar deity and connecting the king with the divine cycle.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Books of Breathing
records.description: Late funerary compositions supporting renewed life and breath for the deceased; distinct from earlier Book of the Dead collections.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Shabaka Stone
records.description: Kushite-period inscribed stone transmitting theology centered on Ptah. Claims of a much earlier original require careful evaluation.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Great Hymn to the Aten
records.description: Amarna royal composition celebrates the solar disk as the source of life. Surviving context is a royal religious reform, not representative of every Egyptian period.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Letters to the Dead
records.description: Written petitions to deceased relatives preserve evidence of ongoing social relations, requests for protection and disputes.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Temple inscriptions
records.description: Late temple walls preserve complex local myths, calendars, theology and ritual formulae, often elaborating earlier traditions.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: On Isis and Osiris
records.description: Greek philosophical treatment by Plutarch preserves a later interpretation of Egyptian religion, including narrative details not uniformly attested in earlier Egyptian texts.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Abydos
records.description: Major center of Osirian pilgrimage and royal mortuary commemoration, associated with festival processions and the tomb of the god.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Busiris
records.description: Delta cult center associated with Osiris and earlier local divine identities; its history helps explain regional Osirian theology.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Heliopolis
records.description: Solar cult and creation theology centered on Ra and Atum; later urban development has obscured much of the ancient site.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Memphis
records.description: Administrative and religious center with major cults of Ptah, sacred Apis bulls and associated funerary gods.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Thebes
records.description: Theban temple network, royal burial landscape and state festivals were major expressions of New Kingdom religion.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Hermopolis Magna
records.description: Middle Egyptian center of Thoth worship and the theological group of eight primordial gods.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Dendera
records.description: Major Hathor sanctuary whose surviving late temple includes celestial imagery, festivals and Osirian chapels.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Edfu
records.description: Ptolemaic temple preserves a rich corpus of Horus myths, cult rituals and royal religious imagery.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Kom Ombo
records.description: Double temple associated with two divine cults; should not be confused with Seth's Nubt near Naqada.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Philae
records.description: Southern island cult complex important in later Isis religion, including worshipers from Nubia. The surviving temples were relocated to Agilkia.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Elephantine
records.description: First Cataract religious center, linked with southern frontier and river inundation.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Bubastis
records.description: Delta city celebrated for the worship of Bastet; festival traditions also appear in Greek testimony.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Sais
records.description: Delta city and major center of Neith, particularly prominent during the Twenty-sixth Dynasty.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Buto
records.description: Delta cult center associated with the cobra goddess and Lower Egyptian royal traditions.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Elkab
records.description: Upper Egyptian center of the vulture goddess and her royal protective role.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Asyut
records.description: Middle Egyptian city with a strong canid deity tradition and important provincial funerary evidence.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Coptos
records.description: Center of Min worship, connected to routes through the eastern desert.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Akhmim
records.description: Upper Egyptian city associated with Min and extensive later religious traditions.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Fayum
records.description: Lake and agricultural region with strong crocodile cult traditions, including multiple local forms of Sobek.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Akhetaten
records.description: New capital established by Akhenaten for the Aten-centered royal cult; its archaeology documents the exceptional reform.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Saqqara
records.description: Mortuary landscape of Memphis, including royal pyramids and burial galleries for sacred Apis bulls.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Deir el-Medina
records.description: Royal tomb workers' community preserves evidence of personal piety, household religion and petitions to deities.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Mendes
records.description: Delta city with ram and fish divine traditions and important local cult identity.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Armant
records.description: Theban-region center of Montu worship and the sacred Buchis bull cult.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Esna
records.description: Late temple inscriptions document rich local theology and creation traditions.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Ankh
records.description: Hieroglyph for life frequently carried by deities or offered to the king; later spiritual uses are separate interpretations.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Djed pillar
records.description: Pillar sign associated with stability and Osirian regeneration; placed on or with funerary equipment as a protective emblem.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Was scepter
records.description: Long staff with distinctive animal-like head and forked base, held by gods and kings; material examples include finds connected with Seth's cult.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Wedjat eye
records.description: Restored eye signifies soundness and protection, commonly expressed in amulets. Modern claims of a universal fractional system require caution.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Uraeus
records.description: Upright cobra on royal and divine headdresses expresses protective and destructive solar power.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Scarab
records.description: Beetle imagery expresses becoming and renewal; heart scarabs have a specialized mortuary function connected with judgment.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Tyet
records.description: Knot-shaped amulet associated with Isis and funerary protection, often made in red material.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Shen ring
records.description: Looped sign associated with enclosure, protection and enduring continuity; related imagery appears in royal contexts.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Cartouche
records.description: Oval enclosure protecting or distinguishing royal names, not a generic magical name seal used identically in every era.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Sistrum
records.description: Rattle associated particularly with Hathor and ritual music; its sound participates in divine celebration and appeasement.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Menat
records.description: Beaded necklace with counterpoise, associated with Hathoric ritual music, protection and renewal.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Crook and flail
records.description: Royal and Osirian emblems of authority, often crossed on the chest of a mummiform figure.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Feather of Ma'at
records.description: Emblem of Ma'at used in divine iconography and mortuary judgment.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Double crown
records.description: Combines the white and red crowns to represent royal sovereignty over Upper and Lower Egypt.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: White crown
records.description: Crown associated with Upper Egypt, appearing in royal and divine representations.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Red crown
records.description: Crown associated with Lower Egypt; the same modern transliteration also refers to red land in other contexts.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Atef crown
records.description: Tall central element with feathers, particularly associated with Osiris and certain other gods.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Winged solar disk
records.description: Protective solar emblem above temple entrances, often incorporating wings and cobras.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Benben stone
records.description: Sacred solar stone linked with first emergence and Heliopolitan creation; related ideas informed obelisk and pyramid imagery.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Obelisk
records.description: Tall tapering stone monument with solar associations, frequently erected in pairs at temples.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Sacred barque
records.description: Portable divine shrine or symbolic vessel used in temple festivals; celestial boats also carry the sun in myth.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Canopic equipment
records.description: Containers and associated guardians protect organs of the deceased; practices and vessel use changed across periods.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Shabti figurines
records.description: Figures associated with performing labor for the deceased, with inscribed examples linked to spell 6.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Offering table
records.description: Provides a surface for sustaining a god or deceased through material and represented offerings; Seti I's dedication to Seth is a concrete example.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Daily temple service
records.description: Authorized personnel cared for the cult image through purification, dressing and offerings; the king was the ideal ritual officiant in formal temple representation.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Temple sanctuary
records.description: Temples housed cult images and ritual institutions. Access and architectural arrangement varied, with central sanctuaries generally restricted.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Personal and household religion
records.description: People sought assistance through amulets, prayers, offerings and domestic shrines; state temples are only one part of the archaeological picture.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Ancestor veneration
records.description: Households maintained relationships with deceased relatives through objects, remembrance, food and requests for intervention.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Divine oracles
records.description: Divine images or their carriers could communicate responses in public and institutional settings; procedures differed by place and period.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Opet festival
records.description: Theban procession of divine images linking Karnak and Luxor and renewing royal legitimacy.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Beautiful Festival of the Valley
records.description: Amun's visit to western Thebes linked temple processions with remembrance and mortuary cult.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Khoiak rites
records.description: Osirian festivals of death and regeneration include ritual images using earth and grain, especially well documented in later temple contexts.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Egyptian New Year
records.description: Renewal of the year was connected with solar, stellar and inundation symbolism; the civil calendar drifted relative to the seasonal year.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Opening of the Mouth
records.description: Ritual complex restores the senses and capacities of a statue or deceased in religious representation; attested in texts and images.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Mummification
records.description: Techniques and associated rites preserved and transformed the body, varying with date, resources and local practice.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Sacred animal cults
records.description: Distinguish particular living divine animals from votive animal offerings and the broader use of animal imagery for gods.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Heka in daily life
records.description: Magic and religious practice overlap in texts for healing, protection and birth. Historical descriptions do not establish supernatural efficacy.
records.period: Ancient Egypt; date varies by evidence

records.title: Greco-Egyptian Hermetica
records.description: Greek and related philosophical and technical writings from the Hellenistic and Roman cultural world develop an Egyptian-associated wisdom figure. They are not simply translations of pharaonic scriptures.
records.period: Later reception / historical method

records.title: Mediterranean Isis cults
records.description: The worship of Isis took new forms across the Greco-Roman Mediterranean, with local rituals and institutions distinct from earlier Egyptian settings.
records.period: Later reception / historical method

records.title: Egyptomania and esoteric Egypt
records.description: European and American esoteric movements repeatedly reimagined ancient Egypt as a source of hidden wisdom, often blending archaeology with their own religious claims.
records.period: Later reception / historical method

records.title: Aleister Crowley and Egyptian imagery
records.description: Thelema draws on reinterpreted Egyptian divine names and symbols, including Nuit, Hadit and Ra-Hoor-Khuit. Their modern theological meanings are not equivalent to the ancient cults of Nut, Horus or other gods.
records.period: Later reception / historical method

records.title: Stele of Revealing
records.description: An ancient funerary stele became a central object in Crowley's account of the origins of Thelema. Its original mortuary purpose and modern interpretation are separate historical contexts.
records.period: Later reception / historical method

records.title: Anton Szandor LaVey
records.description: LaVey founded the Church of Satan in 1966 and developed a modern Satanist philosophy. Its use of names and imagery from earlier cultures does not demonstrate descent from a pharaonic priesthood.
records.period: Later reception / historical method

records.title: Temple of Set
records.description: A modern religious organization established in 1975 following a split with LaVey's Church of Satan. Its interpretation of Set belongs to modern esoteric history, not documented survival of the ancient Nubt temple cult.
records.period: Later reception / historical method

records.title: Contemporary Kemetic religion
records.description: Modern Egyptian-inspired religious communities vary in methods and theology. Reconstruction and personal adaptation should be distinguished from demonstrable ancient practice.
records.period: Later reception / historical method

records.title: Reading the archive
records.description: Egyptian religion spans millennia, with local variation, lost texts and uncertain readings. Entries are reference summaries, not doctrinal instructions; source links are starting points, not proof of every detail.
records.period: Later reception / historical method
